newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: ILO, UNICEF step up fight against child labour.
newsitem.headline: ILO, UNICEF step up fight against child labour.

text.p: The U.N. Children's Fund (UNICEF) and the International Labour Organisation (ILO) said on Tuesday they were stepping up their joint fight against child labour.
The Geneva-based ILO estimates some 73 million children between the ages of 10 and 14 work worldwide -- or 13 per cent of all children in that age group.
Millions more under the age of 10 are also known to be working but the agency said it had no credible statistics.

UNICEF executive director Carol Bellamy and ILO director-general Michel Hansenne signed a letter of intent agreeing to keep up pressure on member states to ratify and implement global labour standards, including the 1973 Minimum Age Convention, according to an ILO statement.

The convention, the ILO's main instrument on child labour, puts 15 as the minimum age for entry into employment. But it leaves loopholes for states to exempt entire sectors or regions and has only been ratified by 49 countries.

The ILO said it was working on a new draft convention "targeting the most abusive and intolerable forms of child labour including child prostitution, work involving toxic substances and other unsafe practices and environments".
ILO spokesman Michel Barton said the process of drafting and negotiating the new instrument would be completed in 1998-99.
"This year there is a renewed offensive on the part of ILO on working children, focussing on the most abusive forms of child labour," he told Reuters.

"ILO believes strongly that child labour cannot be solved in isolation of poverty. However, it can't be (used as) an excuse to delay targeted action against abusive forms which should be eliminated," he added.
